title: Capital One: The Patent and Beyond
subtitle: A self-directed prototype that turned navigation friction into a patented gesture-based interaction model.
summary: Testing showed that customers struggled with too many screens. Van assembled a small team, led the prototype, and helped develop the concept into a patent.

heroImage.title: Patent Figure Sheet
heroImage.caption: Patent figures showing gesture interactions across devices and contexts.

sections.heading: The Story
sections.bodyHtml: Testing showed that customers struggled to find information across too many screens. The team needed a more direct interaction model that reduced navigation and learning.

sections.heading: The Strategic Action
sections.bodyHtml:
Van assembled a small team and led prototype development and technical revisions. The concept earned second place at a hackathon.

He then created a concept video and executive presentation. Collaboration with the legal team developed the idea into a patent.

sections.heading: Impact Beyond the Patent
sections.bodyHtml:
• Customer Win: The concept reduced the learning and effort required to navigate financial information.
  • Technical Win: The gesture model explored interaction across devices and contexts.
  • Organizational Win: A small team turned a usability problem into a working prototype and executive-ready story.
  • Innovation Win: The concept earned hackathon recognition and became a patent.

sections.heading: Published Patent
Strategic Takeaway
sections.bodyHtml: Van turned a usability problem into a prototype, an executive story, and a patent supported by legal partners.
